title: Desk Basis: the Re-Pricing Rate Once a Vacation Package Has Left Its Price Guarantee
content:
The priced places of a re-worked package among the Vacation Package Products carry a re-pricing rate. Two things decide it: whether the product's price-guarantee term has run out, and whether an operator notice stands against the package. The term is counted in whole calendar days from the day after the deposit was taken, and it has run out where that count exceeds the price-guarantee term published against the product booked. An operator notice stands against the package where the count of operator notice lines on its ledger is 1 or more.

**Where the term has run out and a notice stands.** Where the product's price-guarantee term has run out counted in whole calendar days from the day after the deposit was taken and an operator notice stands against the package, the re-pricing rate is the whole of them increased by the re-pricing allowance published for this calculation, which is 2 per cent.

**Where the term has not run out and a notice stands.** Where the product's price-guarantee term has not yet run out counted the same way and an operator notice stands against the package, the re-pricing rate is the whole of them and nothing more.

**Where no operator notice stands.** No increase of this kind is made to the re-pricing rate, whether or not the term has run out.

| Price-guarantee term | Operator notice lines on the package ledger | Re-pricing rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| run out | 1 or more | the whole of them increased by 2 per cent |
| not yet run out | 1 or more | the whole of them and nothing more |
| either | 0 | no increase of this kind |

*On the boundary, hypothetically.* On the All-Inclusive Resort Package the price-guarantee term is 21 calendar days. With an operator notice standing against the package, a count of exactly 21 whole calendar days since the deposit has not exceeded the term, and the rate stands at the whole of them and nothing more. A count of 22 has exceeded it, and priced places of 5,000.00 USD would then be taken at the increased rate, giving 5,100.00 USD.
